JUDGEMENT CALLS (all six CRITICAL sites; none required an override of the tracer default)
  S10 (185,419) JUNCTION. Plain T: the y~419 rail from the source ends on the vertical bar that spans the left ends of the 4kOhm resistor and the 6mH inductor. No dot needed, no hop drawn. A crossing reading is impossible here -- the horizontal wire terminates, it does not continue past x=185, so there is no second branch pair to pass through. Crossing/none would have stranded the whole R||L pair off the source.
  S11 (385,418) JUNCTION. Mirror image of S10 on the right side of the R||L box: the vertical bar joining 0.1 and 3.1 meets the rail that carries on to the current source. T, terminating branch. 'none' would have split the R||L pair off from the shunt resistor and the 3mA source, leaving the pair with only a one-sided connection.
  S12 (436,419) JUNCTION. T: the vertical wire down to the shunt resistor ends on the horizontal y~419 rail; the rail runs straight through left-to-right. Dot score 1.1 (no blob) but a dot is not expected on a T. Reading it as a crossing would put the shunt resistor's top on a net with a single terminal, i.e. a dead branch -- electrically impossible.
  S13 (603,420) JUNCTION. T on the left vertical bar of the 5Ohm/10F box, exactly like S10. The rail from the current source terminates on it. Any other reading strands both the 5Ohm resistor and the 10F capacitor.
  S14 (790,434) JUNCTION. T on the right vertical bar of the 5Ohm/10F box, where the wire that drops to the bottom return rail leaves. Any other reading leaves the current source with no return path to the 20V source.
  S21 (440,605) JUNCTION, deg=5. The shunt-resistor wire comes down from y~587, the sloping bottom return rail crosses horizontally, and the wire continues a few pixels further down into the GND symbol at (439,634). Ink shows a clean 4-way with the vertical passing straight through (dot score 1.8, no hop or jog anywhere on this sheet). Crossing would give ground only to the shunt resistor and the GND symbol -- a 2-terminal dead-end net with no current path -- and would leave the source's return rail floating with no ground reference. Junction is the only sane reading and matches the standard 'ground tap on the return rail' drawing.
